chaining: The two halves do not stack into one cheque: the INR 20 lakh is a grant and the INR 50 lakh is a repayable instrument, so the free portion is the smaller number. Because disbursement runs through an incubator, the practical gate after DPIIT is an incubator selection, which is a second discretionary review.

limits.value: The applicant must be 'A startup, recognized by DPIIT, incorporated not more than 2 years ago at the time of application', and DPIIT recognition requires an Indian incorporated entity, so a person with no Indian company fails before the incubator sees the application.

evidence.proved: 'Up to Rs. 20 Lakhs as grant for validation of Proof of Concept, or prototype development, or product trials'; 'Up to Rs. 50 Lakhs of investment for market entry, commercialization, or scaling up through convertible debentures or debt', quoted

'A startup, recognized by DPIIT, incorporated not more than 2 years ago at the time of application is invited to apply'; 'The Seed Fund will be disbursed to selected startups through eligible incubators across India', quoted
the DPIIT playbook one-pager repeats 'DPIIT recognised startups' and 'Incorporated not more than 2 years ago at the time of application', quoted
the scheme was designed to 'disburse the Seed Fund to 3600 startups through 300 incubators', quoted

notes: The number worth remembering is 20 lakh, because the 50 lakh beside it is debt-like and a reader who takes the pair as a grant overstates the free capacity by a factor of 3.5. DPIIT recognition is not open to foreign founders: recognition requires an entity incorporated in India. Whether the scheme accepts a sole proprietorship is unresolved: the FAQ says 'incorporated', which in Indian usage usually means a company or LLP rather than a proprietorship. The 2-year incorporation clock cannot be paused: it is measured at the time of application. What would settle whether cloud or GPU spend is claimable: the scheme guidelines' eligible-expense list, which has not been read.
